decisions.reason: The cited calligraphic Lp and quotient definitions have real-valued representatives. On a unit-mass singleton, xi=1 and eta=i give h=-i, which has no class in that real quotient. The claimed L1 membership and consequent citation applications are unlicensed, although the intended inner-product construction is valid. Repaired locally by using the real and imaginary components, bounded in absolute value by |h|, and applying real integral invariance and real linearity componentwise.

An arbitrary pointwise bounded operator field need not have measurable norm: on the constant C field over Borel [0,1], T_x=1_A(x)I for non-Borel A has norm 1_A. Step 3.1 correctly proves the claim only under measurable fundamental coefficients. The Definition now explicitly qualifies norm measurability and the ensuing essential-supremum convention by weak measurability, preserving the intended decomposable-operator contract.

reviews.reason: Local repair review: scalar Cauchy-Schwarz applies to the real nonnegative fibre norms and bounds integral |h|. Borel coordinate projections and |Re h|,|Im h| <= |h| supply real L1 classes. Componentwise a.e. invariance, the formula c(u+iv)=(au-bv)+i(av+bu), real linearity, conjugation and the nonnegative zero-integral criterion establish the complex inner-product axioms without AC. Quotient operations use finite unions of Borel null witnesses. No completeness is assumed or added.

Local repair review: finite rational-complex combinations give countably many measurable fibrewise dense tests without AC. Least-index measurable partitions approximate each section; pointwise bounded T_x preserves the pointwise limit, proving the all-section coefficient criterion. Normalized nonzero tests are sphere-dense, with zero tests retained as zero; the norm is the countable supremum of their measurable pairing moduli. This requires weak measurability, now explicit in the Definition. The repaired direct-integral supplier retains its complex pairing and quotient, so its F4 use remains valid. No induced-action existence is assumed by the definition.
